description: Transit-Gym is a simulation and evaluation engine for bus transit systems. A domain-specific language lets subject-matter experts specify scenarios and their parametric variations, covering demand models, route networks and vehicle-to-trip assignments; the tool chain turns them into SUMO configurations, runs origin-destination trip generation and routing, simulates buses and general traffic, and processes outputs such as edge statistics, bus stop events and per-trip bus trajectories. An integrated microscopic energy consumption model estimates the energy cost of transit decisions made by a city's transport agency. It was developed by Vanderbilt University with the University of South Carolina, NREL and the Chattanooga transit authority and described in an arXiv paper of June 2021, with worked examples for Chattanooga, Tennessee, including a 24-hour city scenario and one with origin-destination matrices calibrated against street traffic counts. It is location independent in design but ships at city scale for Chattanooga. The code is free on GitHub under the MIT licence, with a Docker image recipe and a video presentation. Caveats: the last commit was in January 2023, and a full routing run takes tens of minutes on a desktop. Transit-Gym supports capacity planning, optimisation of routes and vehicle assignments, and agent-based evaluation of transit operations, and builds on the SUMO traffic simulator catalogued here.
